sub_indicators.label: EMIS
sub_indicators.subject: digital.rural
sub_indicators.text: Digitalisation of rural primary schools: EMIS
criteria: A dated source states that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only. An annual school census, however it is collected and whatever it is called, does not change this.

A system holding a record for each learner is used by secondary schools only or in some districts, or a national one is contracted or being prepared: staff trained, equipment delivered or an agreement signed. Primary schools do not use it, beyond pilot schools.

A national system holds a record for each primary learner, filled in once a year at enrolment or keyed in elsewhere from the school's paper registers. A minority of primary schools enter attendance or results during the year, or no figure is published.
More than half of primary schools enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, at the school. The figure is a published share, or a count given with its total.
At least 90 per cent of primary schools do so, with attendance entered daily, on a figure published within the past two years. The figure gives the share for rural schools.
